record.original_question: Classify all two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space H^3.

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Classify all two-orbit polyhedra in H3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyhedron in hyperbolic 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ is, in the skeletal sense, a connected geometric realization $P$ of a combinatorial polyhedron (an abstract polytope of rank 3) consisting of vertices (points of $\mathbb{H}^3$), edges (geodesic segments), and faces (finite or infinite skew or planar polygons), in which every edge lies in exactly two faces and the vertex-figure at each vertex is a single (possibly skew) polygon. The symmetry group $G(P)$ is the group of isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$ that map $P$ to itself.

A flag of $P$ is an incident triple (vertex, edge, face). The group $G(P)$ acts on the set of flags of $P$, and $P$ is called a $k$-orbit polyhedron if this action has exactly $k$ orbits. The case $k = 1$ corresponds to regular polyhedra; the case $k = 2$ defines the class of two-orbit polyhedra.

Problem: Classify, up to isometry of $\mathbb{H}^3$, all two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Cunningham–Pellicer and collaborators) has classified two-orbit skeletal polyhedra in Euclidean 3-space (in classes such as 2₀ and 2₂) and chiral polyhedra in several 3-dimensional geometries, but no complete classification of two-orbit polyhedra in hyperbolic 3-space appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On infinite 2-orbit polyhedra in classes 2_0 and 2_2
status_evidence.snippet: Describes all 2-orbit skeletal polyhedra in classes 2_0 and 2_2 in Euclidean 3-space.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of two-orbit polyhedra has been pursued in Euclidean 3-space, not hyperbolic 3-space.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Polyhedra in 3-Dimensional Geometries and from a Petrie–Coxeter Construction
status_evidence.snippet: Studies chiral (a particular type of two-orbit) polyhedra in various 3-dimensional geometries.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results in hyperbolic geometry; full two-orbit classification in H^3 is not established.
